applies_to: all construction statewide (Florida Building Code supersedes local building codes)
quote: As of March 1, 2002, the Florida Building Code, which is developed and maintained by the Florida Building Commission, supersedes all local building codes.
notes: Start of the statewide code. No source found that the 2001-2007 FBC editions set any freeboard; zero is implied because the 2010 FBC (first with R322) still had A-zone floors at the design flood elevation, and FL DEM lists BFE+1 ft as a change new in the 6th Ed. (2017). In 2002-2012 the A-zone elevation was effectively set by local NFIP floodplain ordinances (BFE minimum, local freeboard possible). Before 2002: 1974 state minimum building code law required local governments to adopt one of four model codes (same source); no statewide freeboard.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (FBC Residential); Coastal A Zones excluded (BFE+1 ft there)
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas not designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the design flood elevation. 2. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot (305 mm), or to the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.
date_quote: 2010 Florida Building Code Base Code March 15, 2012
notes: Design flood elevation = BFE unless the community adopts a higher DFE, so no statewide freeboard in ordinary A zones. The 5th Ed. (2014) FBC Residential, effective 2015-06-30 (same date source: 'Florida Building Code 5th Ed (2014) Base Code June 30, 2015'), kept the same R322.2.1 wording (verified at up.codes/viewer/florida/fl-residential-code-2014). V-zone value not extracted (null). Date source is a private contractor's table (medium); JD Supra headline '2010 Florida Building Code Takes Effect March 15, 2012' agrees.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (FBC Residential), all flood hazard areas incl. Coastal A
instrument: 6th Edition (2017) Florida Building Code, Residential, R322.2.1 (and R322.3.2 for V/Coastal A)
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas including flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones, shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot (305 mm), or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. [Summary of changes from the 5th Ed.:] Requires minimum elevation of lowest floor (Zone A) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member of the lowest floor (Zone V and CAZ) is BFE + 1 foot.
date_quote: The 6th Edition of the Florida Building Code will go into effect on December 31, 2017 and will incorporate the latest version of the I-Codes (2015).
notes: Still in force: 7th Ed. (2020) and 8th Ed. (2023) FBC Residential R322.2.1 keep 'base flood elevation plus 1 foot' (verified at up.codes/viewer/florida/fl-residential-code-2020 and -2023); their effective dates were not separately sourced so no extra rows. Local ordinances may require more (BASF 2017 fact sheet: many FL communities require 2-4 ft).

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (NC Residential Code)
instrument: 2012 North Carolina Residential Code (IRC 2009 with NC amendments), R322.2.1
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation Requirements Buildings and structures shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.
date_quote: The 2012 Residential Code was effective from January 1, 2012 through December 31, 2018. The 2009 Residential Code was also valid during a transition period from January 1, 2012 through June 1, 2012.
notes: Earliest NC edition whose flood text was checked. Earlier NC Residential Codes (2002, 2006, 2009; statewide residential code exists since at least 1968 per OSFM archive) were not text-checked; nothing found suggesting a statewide freeboard. V zone R322.3.2: DFE (parallel members) or BFE/DFE (perpendicular) -> 0 ft.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (NC Residential Code)
instrument: 2018 North Carolina Residential Code (IRC 2015 with NC amendments), R322.2.1 / R322.3.2
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation Requirements Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas, including flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones, shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation, or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.
date_quote: The 2018 Residential Code was effective from January 1, 2019 and is currently effective. The 2018 Residential Code was also available during a transition period from July 1, 2018 through December 31, 2018.
notes: NC deleted the 2015 IRC's '+1 foot' (IRC 2015 R322.2.1 reads 'base flood elevation plus 1 foot'). Still in force as of 2026-06-01 (NC Licensing Board update). V zone R322.3.2 also 'base flood elevation or the design flood elevation' -> 0 ft.

instrument: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, 1973 Edition
quote: 1973 Edition - Effective date: September 1, 1973 - Title: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Administrative Amendments, 1973 Edition
notes: Start of statewide code. 0.0 is implied, not text-verified for pre-2012 editions: FEMA RFL (5th ed., 2019) says IRC 2012 and earlier required only BFE/DFE in Zone A, and the VA 2012 VRC (verified) still had no A-zone freeboard; flood elevation content of the BOCA-based 1973-1990s editions was not checked.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (Virginia Residential Code); Coastal A Zones excluded (BFE+1 ft there)
instrument: 2012 Virginia Residential Code (USBC 2012, IRC 2012 with amendments), R322.2.1
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation Requirements Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas not designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the design flood elevation . Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot (305 mm), or to the design flood elevation , whichever is higher.
date_quote: 2012 Edition - Effective Date: July 14, 2014 - Title: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code "USBC" (2012 Edition)
notes: One-year grace: VRC 2012 103.2 lets applicants for one year after the effective date choose the prior edition. V zone (R322.3.2) depends on member orientation: DFE if parallel to wave approach, BFE+1 ft if perpendicular -> v_zone null. Earlier edition 2009 USBC effective 2011-03-01 (same date source), not text-checked.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide (Virginia Residential Code), all flood hazard areas incl. Coastal A
instrument: 2015 Virginia Residential Code (USBC 2015, IRC 2015 with amendments), R322.2.1 / R322.3.2
quote: R322.2.1 Elevation Requirements Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas, including flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones, shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot (305 mm), or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.
date_quote: The 2015 Edition of the Virginia Residential Code (the VRC) was adopted by the Commonwealth of Virginia effective September 4, 2018. The one-year grace period during which either the 2015 Edition or the previous 2012 Edition may be used expires on September 4, 2019. All permit applications submitted on or after September 4, 2019, will be reviewed under the 2015 code edition.
notes: Because of the grace period, permits filed 2018-09-04..2019-09-03 could still use the 2012 VRC (no A-zone freeboard); mandatory for applications from 2019-09-04. DHCD history (2021 VCC) also gives 2015 Edition effective September 4, 2018. Still in force: 2018 VRC (effective 2021-07-01) and 2021 VRC (effective 2024-01-18, per DHCD) keep BFE+1 ft in A zones (verified at up.codes/viewer/virginia/va-residential-code-2018 and irc-2021).

applies_to: residential construction inside municipalities only (no statewide code for unincorporated areas)
instrument: Tex. Local Gov't Code 214.212 (S.B. 365, 77th Leg., 2001): IRC as it existed on May 1, 2001 adopted as municipal residential code
quote: Sec. 214.212. INTERNATIONAL RESIDENTIAL CODE. (a) To protect the public health, safety, and welfare, the International Residential Code, as it existed on May 1, 2001, is adopted as a municipal residential building code in this state. ... SECTION 4. This Act takes effect January 1, 2002
notes: No statewide freeboard. The IRC in force on 2001-05-01 (2000 IRC) had no A-zone freeboard per FEMA RFL ('The 2012 and earlier editions specify ... lowest floors elevated to or above the BFE or DFE') - the 2000 IRC text itself was not read. Municipalities may amend the IRC locally (214.212(c)), so this is a default, not a floor. Before 2002 Texas had no statewide residential building code. Unincorporated areas: Local Gov't Code 233.153 (from 2009-09-01) lets an opting-in county require the IRC 'published as of May 1, 2008' (2006 IRC, no A-zone freeboard) or the county seat's IRC - optional, not statewide.

applies_to: residential construction inside municipalities only; Coastal A Zones excluded (BFE+1 ft under 2012 IRC)
instrument: Tex. Local Gov't Code 214.212 as amended by H.B. 738 (87th Leg., 2021): IRC as it existed on May 1, 2012
quote: (a) To protect the public health, safety, and welfare, the International Residential Code, as it existed on May 1, 2012 [2001], is adopted as a municipal residential building code in this state. ... SECTION 6. This Act takes effect January 1, 2022
date_quote: The 2018 and 2015 editions of the IRC specify the required minimum elevation of lowest floors of dwellings in Zone A is the BFE plus 1 foot or the DFE, whichever is higher. The 2012 and earlier editions specify that buildings must have lowest floors elevated to or above the BFE or DFE, whichever is higher, except in areas designated as Coastal A Zones.
notes: Still no statewide A-zone freeboard: the 2012 IRC requires BFE/DFE in Zone A (FEMA RFL quote in date_quote field). Applies to construction beginning under agreements made on/after 2022-01-01. Municipalities may still amend (add, modify or remove requirements) after a public hearing. Harris County / Houston freeboard is local, not state.

instrument: pre-2007 NYS Uniform Code (start year not sourced)
quote: When there is a base flood elevation available, the lowest floor including any basement, must be at or above the base flood elevation (plus two feet beginning in 2007).
notes: Brochure dated September 2007 (NFIP brochure series, NYS). Implies floor at BFE before the 2007 code. Start year of this period not sourced, so effective_year is null.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide outside New York City (Residential Code of NYS)
instrument: 2007 Residential Code of New York State (19 NYCRR Part 1220; 2003 IRC with NY amendments), R323.1.3.3 and R323.2.1
quote: R323.1.3.3 Freeboard. A freeboard of two feet shall be added where the design flood elevation or other elevation requirements are specified. ... R323.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the design flood elevation plus freeboard as specified in Section R323.1.3.3.
date_quote: Code Effective Date: January 1, 2008 ... the 2007 FCNYS ... buildings that were constructed before January 1, 2008 (the date of which the 2007 FCNYS became effective)
notes: Freeboard text verified (ICC/NYS 2007 RCNYS excerpt, publication date August 2007). Date: NYS DOS code interpretation gives January 1, 2008 as the 2007 Uniform Code effective date (stated for the Fire Code; the Residential Code is part of the same 2007 Uniform Code - not separately confirmed). Any transition period was not checked. A Chenango County brochure dated Sept 2007 says 'plus two feet beginning in 2007' - so the year may be 2007 vs 2008. Exception: no freeboard where no DFE is obtainable and DFE is taken as 3 ft above highest adjacent grade. 2010 RCNYS (R324.1.3.3, same 2-ft wording, verified at up.codes/viewer/new_york/ny-residential-code-2010) and the 2015 IRC + 2017 Uniform Code Supplement (R322.1.4.1.1: 'DFE ... plus a freeboard of 2' (610 mm)') continued it; their effective dates were not separately sourced.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide outside New York City (Residential Code of NYS)
instrument: 2020 Residential Code of New York State (2018 IRC with NY amendments), [NY] R322.2.1 / R322.3.2
quote: [NY] R322.2.1 Elevation Requirements Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas, including flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones , shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 2 feet (610 mm) , or the design flood elevation determined in accordance with Sections R322.1.4 through R322.1.4.1 whichever is higher.
date_quote: The effective date for both codes will be May 12, 2020. ... So prior to May 12, 2020, the Uniform Code will continue to include the 2015 I-Codes, as amended by the 2017 Uniform Code Supplement. ... On and after May 12, 2020, the Uniform Code and Energy Code will include the 2020 NYS Code Books with no grace period.
notes: No change in A-zone freeboard (2 ft continued); row kept to document continuity. AO zones: depth number + 1 ft.

applies_to: new 1-2 family dwellings statewide outside New York City; +18 in sea-level rise added in flood hazard areas adjacent to tidal areas
instrument: 2025 Residential Code of New York State (2024 IRC with NY amendments), [NY] R306.1.4 and R306.2.1
quote: [NY] R306.1.4 Establishing the Design Required Flood Elevation At a minimum, the required flood elevation shall be the higher of the following: The base flood elevation ... plus: 2 feet (610 mm) of freeboard , and A sea level rise of 18 inches (457 mm) in flood hazard areas adjacent to tidal areas.
date_quote: December 31, 2025 [implementation date for the 2025 Residential Code of New York State]; the Code Council approved a transition window allowing compliance with either the 2025 or the 2020 Uniform Code in the interim period (summary of the DOS page, not verbatim).
notes: A-zone freeboard stays 2 ft; in tidal-adjacent areas the requirement becomes BFE + 2 ft + 1.5 ft SLR (3.5 ft total). Effective date also appears in the code text: R102.6 'the "effective date of this code" shall be deemed to be December 31, 2025' (up.codes chapter 1). Date quote came via a page summary, not a verbatim read.

applies_to: new buildings incl. 1-2 family dwellings in New York City (NYC Building Code Appendix G + ASCE 24 as modified by BC G501.1)
instrument: 2008 NYC Building Code (Local Law 33 of 2007), Appendix G, G304.1.1 and ASCE 24-05 Table 2-1 as modified by G501.1
quote: The current reference standard American Society of Civil Engineers ("ASCE") 24, as modified by Section BC G501.1 of the New York City Building Code, does not mandate freeboard above the Base Flood Elevation ("BFE") for buildings in Structural Occupancy Category I or II.
date_quote: Application filed between July 1, 2008 and July 1, 2009: apply the 2008 Code, or apply the 1968 Code (with administration/enforcement/safety sections of the 2008 Code). Application filed after July 1, 2009: 2008 Code applies. (summary of the DOB page)
notes: 1-2 family dwellings are Structural Occupancy Category II, so floor at BFE (G304.1.1: 'elevated to at or above the design flood elevation specified in ASCE 24, Table 2-1'). Optional 1968 code until 2009-07-01. NYC is not under the NYS Residential Code's 2-ft rule (NYC has its own code; the 2013 DOB rule says it was brought 'into alignment with ... New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code (2010) by requiring two feet of freeboard for 1- and 2-family dwellings', implying the state rule did not apply in NYC before). Pre-2008 (1968 code) flood provisions not checked. V-zone value not extracted.

applies_to: new / substantially improved 1-2 family dwellings in NYC special flood hazard areas
instrument: 1 RCNY 3606-04 (NYC DOB rule amending ASCE 24 Tables 2-1/4-1 as modified by BC G501.1) - post-Sandy mandatory freeboard rule
quote: This rule became effective on January, 31, 2013. ... TABLE 2-1 MINIMUM ELEVATION OF THE TOP OF LOWEST FLOOR RELATIVE TO DESIGN FLOOD ELEVATION (DFE)-A-ZONES ... II (1- and 2-family dwellings) DFE=BFE+ 2 ft ... The rule brings the New York City Building Code into alignment with the latest edition of New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code (2010) by requiring two feet of freeboard for 1- and 2-family dwellings
notes: V zones (Table 4-1) also BFE+2 ft for 1-2 family dwellings (verified in up.codes NYC 2008 code Appendix G, which notes the 2013 rule). Rule later repealed (effective 2016-08-12) because the content moved into the 2014 NYC Building Code Appendix G, where Table 2-1 gives DFE = BFE + 2 ft for all occupancy categories I-III (up.codes nyc-building-code-2014); Local Law 43 of 2021 (eff. 2022-04-19) and the 2022 code keep BFE+2 ft. Local Law 96 of 2013 did NOT change freeboard: it adopted FEMA preliminary FIS/FIRMs (PFIRMs, governing until FIRMs dated after 2014-05-01) and switched the city datum to NAVD88; its effective date was 30 days after FEMA issued the next preliminary FIS. Emergency Executive Order (Jan 2013) on ABFEs not checked.
